context: Your closest friend quietly wronged a stranger, and only you saw it. Speaking up would end the friendship.
option_a: Protect your friend — loyalty is sacred, and you don't turn on your own.
option_b: Tell the truth — what's fair to the stranger doesn't bend for friendship.

context: You're dividing a windfall among a group. One member is in real need but contributed the least.
option_a: Give the needy one more — relieving real suffering outweighs strict shares.
option_b: Split it by contribution — fair means people get what they earned.

context: Your aging parent makes you promise to keep a secret that is quietly harming your sibling.
option_a: Break the secret — preventing harm to your sibling comes first.
option_b: Keep your word to your parent — family trust is a bond you don't break.

context: A long-standing rule in your community feels pointless, and quietly ignoring it would harm no one.
option_a: Follow it anyway — rules hold because people keep them, sensible or not.
option_b: Ignore it — no one should obey a rule that serves no real purpose.

context: Someone you love is making a reckless choice that will likely hurt only themselves.
option_a: Let them — it's their life and their right to choose, even badly.
option_b: Intervene hard — you don't stand by while someone you love self-destructs.

context: A practice you find degrading is something others do privately, harming no one.
option_a: Some things are simply beneath us, harm or not, and shouldn't be normalized.
option_b: If it harms no one, it's nobody's business but their own.

context: Your boss gives you an order that's perfectly legal but that you believe is unjust to a coworker.
option_a: Resist it — you don't carry out something you believe is unfair.
option_b: Follow the chain — order breaks down if everyone overrides their boss.

context: Management asks your team to report on each other's mistakes.
option_a: Protect your team — you don't inform on your own to the bosses.
option_b: Comply — the institution's rules outrank clubby solidarity.

context: A rule requires you to turn away someone in genuine need because they lack the right paperwork.
option_a: Help them anyway — a person's suffering outweighs a form.
option_b: Follow procedure — rules exist so help is consistent, not arbitrary.

context: A grieving family wants a burial ritual you find unsanitary but that is deeply meaningful to them.
option_a: Hold the line on what's clean and proper — some standards shouldn't bend.
option_b: Let them grieve their way — their comfort matters more than your discomfort.

context: Ending a special protection would free everyone to compete, but the disadvantaged would fall further behind.
option_a: Free the field — let everyone rise or fall by their own effort.
option_b: Keep the protection — a fair start matters more than a free-for-all.

context: You can give a job to a stranger who's clearly more deserving, or to a loyal old friend.
option_a: Hire on merit — the best person should get it, friendship aside.
option_b: Hire your friend — loyalty earned over years counts for something real.

context: Following the official process exactly would produce an outcome you know is unjust.
option_a: Follow the process — its legitimacy is what keeps outcomes fair over time.
option_b: Override it — a just result matters more than a tidy procedure.

context: A treatment that would relieve real suffering involves something many people find morally repugnant.
option_a: Relieve the suffering — easing real pain outweighs a taboo.
option_b: Some lines shouldn't be crossed even to do good.

context: Defending your country's interest abroad would mean real harm to innocent foreigners.
option_a: Your own people come first — that is what loyalty means.
option_b: Innocent lives count the same wherever they're born.

context: A capable leader could do great good, but only with powers that bypass the usual checks.
option_a: Never — no good outcome is worth handing one person unchecked power.
option_b: Sometimes decisive, unencumbered authority is exactly what a moment needs.

context: A large gift arrives from a source many people consider morally tainted.
option_a: Refuse it — money from something rotten stays rotten.
option_b: Take it and do real good with it — the help outweighs its origin.

context: A family tradition you personally find distasteful is precious to your relatives.
option_a: Honor it — family bonds matter more than your distaste.
option_b: Bow out — you won't take part in something you find degrading.

context: The rule demands a punishment far harsher than the person in front of you deserves.
option_a: Apply the rule as written — consistency is the whole point.
option_b: Temper it with mercy — the human being matters more than the letter.

context: People are free to consume art and media you believe is morally corrosive.
option_a: Their choice — freedom includes the freedom to indulge.
option_b: Some things degrade a culture and shouldn't be celebrated.

context: A scarce, life-improving good must be allocated: by equal-chance lottery, or to those willing to pay.
option_a: Lottery — an equal shot is the fairest way to share it.
option_b: Let the market decide — people should be free to trade for what they value.

context: A public mandate would protect the vulnerable, but it constrains everyone's freedom to choose.
option_a: Mandate it — protecting the vulnerable is worth the constraint.
option_b: Leave it to choice — you can't force people, even for their own good.

context: Your employer is quietly underpaying a group; exposing it helps them but betrays the trust you were given.
option_a: Stay loyal — you don't air your own house's dirty laundry.
option_b: Expose it — fairness to the underpaid outweighs corporate loyalty.

context: A tradition asks the young to defer to their elders' judgment even when they sincerely disagree.
option_a: Defer — wisdom and order flow from respecting those who came before.
option_b: Think for yourself — age alone doesn't make someone right.

context: In a crowded clinic you must choose: treat the sickest first, or treat people in the order they arrived.
option_a: Sickest first — relieve the worst suffering, queue be damned.
option_b: First come, first served — everyone waits their fair turn.

context: A superior orders you to do something that would betray your own team's trust.
option_a: Obey — the order stands above team loyalty.
option_b: Protect your people — you won't betray those who trust you.

context: Someone wins fair and square by the rules, but with methods you find sleazy.
option_a: They earned it by the rules — reward the result.
option_b: How you win matters — sleaze shouldn't be rewarded.

context: You can leave your hometown and family to chase your own dream, or stay out of a sense of duty.
option_a: Go — your one life is yours to live.
option_b: Stay — you owe something to the people who raised you.

context: A just exception to the rules for one person would be unfair to everyone who followed them.
option_a: No exceptions — fair means the same rules for all.
option_b: Make the exception — this person's situation is genuinely different.

context: Speech that's hateful but harmless collides with a community's norm of civility.
option_a: Protect the speech — freedom has to include the offensive.
option_b: Uphold the norm — some standards of conduct deserve to be enforced.
